insights.insight: Ad tech charges $5–$150 CPA to infer a purchase may have happened; a verified receipt confirms it did, at ~$0.10 per signal — a 50–200x cost delta that eliminates the attribution problem rather than approximating around it.

Cookies are gone, fingerprinting is degrading, and first-party data is blind beyond a single ecosystem — the protocol produces identity-free, cryptographically signed purchase signals that none of the incumbent alternatives can replicate.

insights.topic: Digital commerce receipts entering the pipeline
insights.insight: Amazon, Shopify, Stripe, Gumroad, and Paddle now appear in the verified receipt window alongside Walmart and Target, confirming the verifiable signal universe has expanded beyond physical retail into DTC and SaaS commerce.

Amazon knows your Amazon purchases; Walmart knows yours at Walmart; neither sees cross-retailer behavior — at 5,226 verified receipts across 15+ metro areas and multiple retail categories, this protocol captures the cross-ecosystem signal both are structurally blind to.

10.3% of receipts are unresolved to a merchant category but carry a $272 average basket — 6.7x the grocery average — indicating high-ticket and B2B transactions are flowing through but failing standard taxonomy, a data quality gap worth watching for brands in those verticals.

insights.topic: Dining overtaking grocery in spend share
insights.insight: Restaurants-dining has pulled ahead of grocery-supermarkets in both receipt count (263 vs. 269, near parity) and total spend ($14,571 vs. $10,898) within the 14-day window — a category rotation that CPG and QSR brands should track as a leading behavioral shift.
